text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian-Syrian talks in Latakia concentrated on coordinating efforts to deal with obstacles to peace. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said the position taken by the Jerusalem committee today will be based on the resolution of the recent Islamic summit in Islamabad.
- President Hosni Mubarak signs the new legislation on the inheritance of leases for non-residential properties.

- Cabinet Affairs Minister Talaat Hammad said the government expected the inflow of capital to increase in the coming months afetr new incentives and guarantees for investment are in place. He indicated that new ways to settle investment disputes are being prepared, either by agreement with the investor or in the framework of agreements signed by Egypt and other countries or through the Cairo regional centre for commercial arbitration.

- John Westley, director of USAID in Egypt, denied that the United States had reduced military aid to Egypt. He said he had not received any notification of this from Washington. The aid runs at $1.3 billion (a year).
- Mubarak will attend the opening of the economic conference of the ruling National Democratic Party on Saturday.

- Manpower and Employment Minister Ahmed el-Amawi said the first instalment of compensation for Egyptian victims of the Gulf War will be disbursed at the beginning of May. The amount is $58.350 million and 23,334 people are eligible to receive it.

- The executive committee of the Social Fund for Development has decided from March 1 to cut the interest on its loans to small projects from eight percent to seven percent for new projects and from 10 percent to nine percent for existing projects. It is doubling the period of tax exemption to 10 years from five years.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri returned from Damascus. Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Palestine are submitting an Arab draft to the Jerusalem committee meeting in Rabat.
- Mubarak will make a speech to teachers on teachers' day today. Education Minister Hussein Kamel Bahaeddin will deliver it on his behalf.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said the draft law on investment incentives and guarantees confirms all the guarantees which Egypt has offered to insure capital against nationalisation and appropriation.

- Industry Minister Soleiman Reda said the new discovery of iron ore southeast of Aswan contains 278 million tonnes concentrated in two areas -- one with proven reserves of up to 73 million tonnes and containing up to 66 percent ferric oxide. The other has reserves of up to 305 million tonnes (sic) and the concentration of ferric oxide in it is between 50 and 62 percent. Other areas are still being prospected.
- Egypt leads today a move to save Jerusalem.
- EgyptAir starts flying Libyan pilgrims from Tripoli tomorrow and from Benghazi on Sunday. Forty-five flights will move 11,000 Libyan pilgrims.
